## source_to_kb

**P3** hub standing_patient_pay_transfer (selection, due-day/first-funds-day posting, effect, tool table = contract). Baseline → patient_pay_transfer_computation: amount formula, caps (open balance; available balance; Medicaid-payee PNA), open balance incl. reductions, available balance, credit formula (payments on other charges + other-reason reductions + reconciliation + not-eligible − other charges, ≥ 0, pooled), defaults (month's patient pay = charge as billed; credited amounts = posted trueups / not-eligible reductions), and the source's own sentence "A reduction posted on the named charge itself records the same difference … changes nothing" (verbatim in the source baseline). Factors: named_month_standing → named_month_case_standing; named_month_amount → named_month_patient_pay_amount ("first row that fits decides"); credited_reconciliation_amount → pending_reconciliation_credit; credited_not_eligible_amount → not_eligible_month_credit (month-count conventions stated). Every tier exact. Source-side note S4: the P3 source baseline embeds the month-standing ladder before the standard-method override; the KB renders only the standard method (correct).
**P4** hub bed_hold_overcharge_return (rule sentence 1, scope, effect, tool table = contract, Q&A "the bed-hold charge is not changed"). Baseline → bed_hold_return_computation: selection, steps 1–5, first chargeable night (latest of three, election rationale), last held day, nightly rate due with "where no room tier can be priced, the charge's own daily rate", room tier = agreement tier, all nights at the schedule in effect on the billing date (2026 / 2025 split by billing date), standard notice rule (every night), whole excess; rate table (12 params). Factors: hold_notice_night → bed_hold_notice_first_night (3 tiers; departure date = leave start); hold_room_tier → bed_hold_room_tier_priced (3 tiers); hold_refund_order → bed_hold_refund_sequence (3 tiers; other payments = payments naming it less trust transfers naming it); **hold_night_schedule → bed_hold_night_rate_schedule: see K1.**
**P5** hub coinsurance_overcharge_return (rule sentence 1, scope, effect, tool table = contract). Baseline → coinsurance_return_computation: selection, steps 1–5 incl. the multi-stretch booking-error rule, the share window by supplemental effective date (incl. secondary-party charged days), defaults (all priced days to the covered end, no center-borne day, charge's own rate, 100 % share, whole excess). Factors: block_covered_end → coinsurance_block_covered_end; center_borne_days → uncertified_center_borne_days (initial recertification day defined; figure in Medicare corpus "Day 14"); block_plan_share → block_supplemental_share; service_year_rate → block_service_year_rate; coinsurance_refund_order → coinsurance_payment_refund_sequence. Every tier exact.
**P6** hub spare_amount_withdrawal (request semantics, payment by check above petty cash, three prerequisite sentences, tool table = contract). Baseline → spare_amount_computation (available balance, ≥ 0, RND once; nothing kept back by default — rendered silently as "the spare amount … is the available balance"). Every tier exact; product figures (PNA 45.00, VA 90.00 → medicaid patient_pay_deductions_schedule; cable 42.00 → ancillary schedule) named and findable.
**Prerequisites of P6** (all form state, value_input), each `policy_source` verbatim in spare_amount_withdrawal §When the spare amount is worked out, connectives intact ("not worked out until", "fixed only after", "Before … must carry"), in no other document:

The source tier is "the schedule in effect on the date the charge was billed (the charge's own daily rate for a charge billed before 2025-07-01)"; the parenthetical value is not in the factor document (it sits only in the computation memo), so the factor's ladder is not carried in full in its own document: for a charge billed before 2025-07-01 the factor document names a schedule the corpus does not contain. No effect on this task's numbers (the charge was billed 2026-07-03; its nights take tier 2). P3, P5, P6 and base policies: PASS.
